title: Smooth scalar tests detect locally integrable functions almost everywhere
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $m\geq1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ be open, and let $f:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf C$ be locally Lebesgue integrable on $U$, meaning that $f$ is Lebesgue measurable on $U$ and each $x\in U$ has a neighborhood $N$ with $\int_{N\cap U}|f(t)|\,dt<\infty$. Suppose that for every smooth real-valued function $g$ on $\mathbf R^m$ whose topological support (the closure of its nonzero locus) is compact and contained in $U$, one has $\int_{\mathbf R^m}g(t)f(t)\,dt=0$. Then $f=0$ Lebesgue almost everywhere on $U$, meaning outside a set of Lebesgue measure zero in $U$.
